note: The reading the top item of runs/next.md asks for: the same profile that answers 'is the pass's cost in the kernels' own spans or in the space between them'. Two new lines are the point of it. (1) `total T ms (sum of per-dispatch spans, 1280x720), N dispatches, a barrier after every launch` - N is the dispatch count the plan has been quoting as 120 by hand, and T is the instrument's old number, so it should land near r2026-11-08-profile-720p's 3.620 ms; a T far from that (say 1.7x) is the contended-card signature and the run tells nothing. (2) `production schedule (counter chaining): N dispatches, GPU X ms (min of 7, same graph and size, no client in the loop)` - the graph run on the route the worker actually ships (counter chaining, no barrier between launches), GPU-timestamped, for the first time outside a live frame. Read, in this order: the card gate (gpu_before / gpu_after / idle_waited_s - BUSY before or a non-zero idle wait means quote nothing); then T against 3.620; then X against the worker's own live line for the same network - the large network's `network+composite` reads ~9.9 ms at 1080p in the plan's table, which includes the pre-network dispatches (history expand, resize, proxy expand, preprocess) that the profile never counts; then the difference T - X, which is what a barrier after every launch costs and is the one quantity the 120-kernel table cannot show. Above ~0.3 ms the barrier is a real cost and the next change is in the launch path; inside the 0.03 ms noise bar the cost is the dispatches' own work and the next change is a kernel row. Quote the two lines verbatim in the reading - the numbers matter more than the prose. If the run dies with `vkQueueWaitIdle(queue_) failed: -4`, stop queueing and report the card.
